paragraphs.text: Dennis Rongo's plugin collection for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
# dsh-plugins
Dennis Rongo's plugin collection for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — an MIT agent harness where every capab
gin collection for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — an MIT agent harness where every capability is a plugin.
Everything here is built on the harness's public seams: cordis service keys, the Typert host/client
bridge, `shell.*` slots, the system-prompt section registry, and `ctx.cmdlineArgs`. No forks, no pat
ched launcher, no vendored harness code.
**Both surfaces are supported.** Every plugin runs unchanged under the `dsh` CLI *and* under **DSH D
esktop** — a community desktop wrapper that ships the harness pre-packaged with multi-provider model
support ("Any model, zero setup"), for Windows and macOS. It is an independent project, not affilia
el, zero setup"), for Windows and macOS. It is an independent project, not affiliated with DeepSeek.
The desktop keeps its own `DSH_HOME` (`%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness` on Windows) with its own profi
les, so you install a plugin once per profile on whichever surface you use. Nothing here is CLI-spec
ific: the same package, the same `cordis.patch.yml` row, and the same `/api` endpoints serve both.
> **Status:** works with **DSH Desktop `0.10.0`** (dsh `0.1.7-rc.2`) and the **`dsh` CLI at `0.1.5-r
c.3`** — both surfaces verified live, all six host services answering. Desktop `0.10.0` needs the co
dec-fix releases of the host plugins (see the table below); older Desktop/CLI versions keep working,
since the fix is backward-compatible. dsh is a fast-moving `0.1.x` dev preview that promises breaki
ng changes — re-verify against your installed version, and read Harness compatibility for what has b

roken so far and what is still open.
>

### What broke, and when

**2026-10-03 — DSH Desktop 0.10.0 (dsh 0.1.7-rc.2).** Two changes, one of them
ours:

1. **Every host service refused to register, and the harness refused to boot.**
`dsh-typert-loader`

0.1.7 changed the strict-codec contract: a codec is no
longer a `schema` (a zod v4 instance the load

er validates and the gateway
parses through) but a **`create()` factory** returning the schema, whic

h
`requireStrictCodec` demands as a function and the gateway calls as
`codec.create().parse(value)`

(`dsh-api-gateway`, `decode()`). All six host
manifests here predate that, so `validateTypertManifes

t` threw for the first
invocation of each, `auditStartupEntries` failed the entry, and the host
exit
ed before serving anything:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The fix carries **both** members — `schema` for dsh ≤0.1.5 (whose loader
requires a zod instance and

whose gateway parses `codec.schema.parse(...)`)
and `create: () => schema` for 0.1.7+ — in the one

`descriptor()` builder
each plugin's `src/remote.ts` shares between its host and client faces.
Neith

er era's validator rejects the other's member, so one build serves both
surfaces and stays backward-

compatible; the CLI at 0.1.5-rc.3 was still
booting on `schema` the whole time. Fixed in **`dsh-git`

0.5.1,
`dsh-hooks` 0.2.1, `dsh-memory` 0.1.3, `dsh-mission-control` 0.5.2,
`dsh-plan-board` 0.3.2,

`dsh-todo` 0.5.3** — until those are published,
market installs of the older releases still fail to

boot on Desktop 0.10.0.
Verified by importing every built manifest through the Desktop bundle's own

`validateTypertManifest`, then scratch-booting the bundled harness against a
throwaway `DSH_HOME` wi

th the profile plugins junctioned at this repo: all
six services answer `ok:true` on 0.1.7-rc.2.

2. **Plugin deployment moved to enforced "generations" — dev links no longer
reach the Desktop.** 0.

10.0 migrates profile plugins into
`profiles/.generations/live/<pkg>+<version>+<hash>/node_modules/<

pkg>`
snapshots, with the profile's `node_modules/@dennisrongo/<pkg>` symlinked
there and `dsh.deskt

op.generationProjection` in the profile manifest naming
